name: Deadlock - Indefinite Process Wait vs Circular Lock Dependency
voiceSnippet: In my production incident last year, four backend processes were stuck waiting on each other indefinitely because each process needed a database lock held by another process in the group.
documentSnippet: Deadlock is a concurrency condition in which an execution thread is blocked permanently awaiting a resource held by another blocked thread in a closed dependency cycle.

name: Paging - Physical Frame Partitioning vs RAM Allocation Blocks
voiceSnippet: We chop up the physical RAM into equal little boxes called frames so the operating system can map any virtual page anywhere without worrying about finding contiguous chunks.
documentSnippet: Physical memory is partitioned into fixed-size storage units designated as page frames to eliminate external fragmentation and facilitate non-contiguous allocation.

name: Quicksort - Pivot Reordering vs Key Partitioning
voiceSnippet: You pick one element as your pivot, and then you shuffle everything smaller over to the left side and everything larger over to the right side.
documentSnippet: The partition algorithm rearranges array elements in-place such that elements strictly less than the selected pivot precede it, and elements greater than or equal succeed it.

name: Cache Hit - Local Fast Memory Match vs Low-Latency Buffer Lookup
voiceSnippet: When the CPU requests a word and finds it right there waiting in the fast on-chip SRAM without needing to crawl out to main memory, that's what we celebrate as a cache hit.
documentSnippet: A cache hit occurs when a memory access reference matches an active tag inside the cache hierarchy, servicing the request with minimal latency cycles.

name: Starvation - Low Priority Inaction vs Indefinite Postponement
voiceSnippet: If high priority jobs keep showing up constantly, the poor low priority task sits at the back of the queue forever and never gets dispatched.
documentSnippet: Starvation, or indefinite postponement, denotes a scheduling anomaly wherein a runnable process is perpetually denied dispatch due to continuous higher-priority resource acquisition.

name: Deadlock - Database Lock War Story vs Dining Philosophers
voiceSnippet: In our payment processing service, Service A held customer row 101 and requested 102, while Service B held 102 and requested 101, freezing our gateway.
documentSnippet: Consider five philosophers seated around a circular table with five chopsticks. If every philosopher concurrently picks up the left chopstick, a circular wait deadlock is established.

name: Producer-Consumer - Bakery Queue vs Bounded Buffer Array
voiceSnippet: Think of a busy bakery: the baker bakes fresh loaves and puts them onto the display rack, while shoppers take loaves off the rack as long as it's not empty.
documentSnippet: The bounded-buffer synchronization pattern uses two counting semaphores: empty (initialized to N) and full (initialized to 0) to manage circular array buffer slots.

name: Recursion - Russian Dolls vs Factorial Call Tree
voiceSnippet: Recursion is exactly like opening a Russian matryoshka doll: you open one, find a slightly smaller version inside, and keep going until you hit the solid baby doll at the core.
documentSnippet: In computing factorial(N) recursively, factorial(4) generates an invocation chain 4 * factorial(3) down to the base case condition N == 1, which returns 1.

name: Docker Containerization - Teacher Debugging Incident (Voice Only)
voiceSnippet: When we containerized our monolithic service with Docker, we ran into an issue where the container's PID 1 was not reaping zombie processes, which crashed the pod after 48 hours.
documentSnippet: Operating systems manage processes through standard fork-exec mechanisms and maintain process control blocks in the kernel data structures.

name: Git Commit Amend - Team Sprint Practice (Voice Only)
voiceSnippet: In our team sprint reviews, remember to always use git commit --amend if you only missed a typo in your last commit, instead of cluttering git log with useless fixup commits.
documentSnippet: Version control systems record project history through a directed acyclic graph of immutable commit snapshots.

name: Postgres Composite Index Ordering (Voice Only)
voiceSnippet: Always put the equality column first in your composite index and the range column second, or Postgres will completely ignore the second column during index scans.
documentSnippet: Relational databases use B-tree indices to provide logarithmic search performance for equality and range query predicates.

name: Master Theorem Continuous Case 3 Lemma (Document Only)
voiceSnippet: For divide and conquer runtimes, just use the Master Theorem shortcut: compare log_b(a) with the exponent of f(n) to determine which term dominates.
documentSnippet: Lemma 4.3 (Master Theorem Regularity Condition): In Case 3, if f(n) = Omega(n^(log_b(a) + epsilon)), there must exist a constant c < 1 and sufficiently large n such that a * f(n/b) <= c * f(n).

name: Intel 8086 Hardware Pinout Voltage Specification (Document Only)
voiceSnippet: The 8086 processor uses segmented memory addresses where the physical address is formed by shifting the segment register 4 bits left and adding the offset.
documentSnippet: Pin 33 (MN/MX) configures the 8086 for Minimum Mode (tied to +5V) or Maximum Mode (tied to GND). VCC is supplied at Pin 40 with a tolerance of +/- 10% operating voltage.

name: B-Tree Disk Block Overhead Formula (Document Only)
voiceSnippet: We love B-trees because they have high branching factor, meaning a search only needs two or three disk accesses even for millions of records.
documentSnippet: Given block size B, key size K, and record pointer size P, the maximum order M of an internal B-tree node is derived by: M * P + (M - 1) * K <= B.

name: Classification Conflict - Pedagogical Course Override
voiceSnippet: For this course and our mid-term exam, remember that we treat starvation as a special type of deadlock where one process is frozen while others progress.
documentSnippet: In formal operating system theory, starvation and deadlock are strictly distinct anomalies: deadlock involves a circular wait with zero progress, whereas starvation permits system progress while individual threads suffer delay.

name: Factual Conflict - IPv6 Base Header Size
voiceSnippet: Remember that the IPv6 base header is streamlined to exactly 32 bytes to ensure fast hardware routing.
documentSnippet: The base IPv6 packet header has a fixed length of exactly 40 octets (320 bits), consisting of Version, Traffic Class, Flow Label, Payload Length, Next Header, Hop Limit, and two 128-bit addresses.

name: Procedural Conflict - Two-Phase Locking Shrinking Phase
voiceSnippet: During the shrinking phase of 2PL, a transaction can still acquire shared read locks as long as it releases all its exclusive write locks first.
documentSnippet: The Two-Phase Locking (2PL) protocol strictly mandates that once a transaction enters the shrinking phase and releases any lock, it cannot obtain any further locks of any type (shared or exclusive).

name: Definitional Conflict - ACID Isolation Levels
voiceSnippet: In our database curriculum, Read Committed isolation completely prevents non-repeatable reads because it re-reads data from disk.
documentSnippet: Under Read Committed isolation, non-repeatable reads remain possible because concurrent transactions can commit modifications between successive reads.

name: Polysemous False Match - Memory Bank vs Financial Bank
voiceSnippet: We configure memory bank interleaving across consecutive addresses so multiple RAM channels can service memory requests simultaneously.
documentSnippet: The Central Bank of India increased interest rates across regional commercial bank reserves to control quarterly inflation.

name: Polysemous False Match - BST Rebalancing vs Decision Tree
voiceSnippet: Whenever an AVL tree becomes unbalanced after an insertion, we perform a left or right rotation around the pivot node to maintain O(log N) height.
documentSnippet: In a decision tree classifier, each internal node represents a feature attribute test, and branches represent split outcomes calculated using Gini impurity.

name: Polysemous False Match - Mutex Lock vs Canal Navigation Lock
voiceSnippet: Acquire the mutex lock before entering the critical section, and release the lock immediately upon leaving so other threads aren't delayed.
documentSnippet: The Panama Canal uses a system of water locks to raise and lower cargo vessels across Gatun Lake between ocean elevations.

name: Partial Overlap - Deadlock Prevention vs Complete Deadlock Handling
voiceSnippet: Today we focus specifically on deadlock prevention: invalidating mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, and circular wait.
documentSnippet: Deadlock handling strategies encompass prevention (invalidating conditions), avoidance (Banker's algorithm), detection (resource graph cycles), and recovery (process termination).

name: Partial Overlap - TCP Congestion Control vs TCP Flow and Congestion
voiceSnippet: We are looking only at TCP congestion control today: slow start, congestion avoidance, and multiplicative decrease when packet loss occurs.
documentSnippet: TCP transmission regulation involves flow control (protecting the receiving endpoint buffer using receiver window rwnd) and congestion control (protecting the intermediate network using cwnd).

voiceSnippet: Database concurrency control is about ensuring multiple users can read and write simultaneously without corrupting the database state.

name: One-To-Many - Software Testing vs Testing Levels
voiceSnippet: Software testing validates that our system behaves as expected across different granularities before deploying to production.
documentSnippet: The V-Model specifies testing levels: Unit Testing verifies isolated functions, Integration Testing verifies module boundaries, and System Testing verifies end-to-end specifications.
